Maya (infra): Quick on-call cheat sheet for spot/preemptible events — short checklist we can follow before escalating. Keeping this minimal for fast scanning.

Sam (oncall): nice, can you put the triage steps first?

Maya (infra): 1) Confirm scope: check ops-bot alert + `kubectl get nodes -l pool=spot -o wide` and `gcloud compute instances list --filter='preemptible'` / `aws ec2 describe-spot-instance-requests` depending on cloud.

ops-bot: [ALERT] preemptible-spot-evac noticed 18% node churn in eu-west-1 (affected pool: spot-gpu-large). See /alerts/1961234567

Jordan (eng-infra): If node count dropped < 5% and pods are evicted, it's usually auto-recovered by autoscaler. Watch for crashloops.

Maya (infra): 2) Check workload impact: `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Failed -A` and `kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces | grep Evicted` then filter by model-serving namespaces (prod-models, training).

Kai (SRE): Tip: prioritize low-latency endpoints. If prod-models svc shows degraded pods, start traffic shift.

Maya (infra): 3) Immediate mitigation (fast):
- For small surface (<= 5% pods): allow autoscaler 3–7m to refill.
- For larger impact or sustained >5m: cordon affected nodes and drain safely: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`.
- If draining large sets, do in batches of 4 nodes to avoid thundering herd.

Sam (oncall): What about stateful jobs?

Maya (infra): Stateful: try to reschedule manually to dedicated GPU pools: label selectors help. Example: `kubectl patch deployment my-model -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"preferred-pool":"dedicated-gpu"}}}}}'` or use routing config in canary controller.

Jordan (eng-infra): 4) Fallback routing: our runtime supports route-level fallback to `dedicated-fallback` via console or CLI: `rictl routes update --service models-api --fallback dedicated-fallback`. Do this if latency errors > 5% for 2 consecutive 1m windows.

Maya (infra): 5) Cost guardrails to keep in mind (do not change on-call):
- Maintain min_spot_reserve = 20% for critical clusters.
- Don't raise spot utilization above 75% without approval.
- If we flip traffic to dedicated, notify finance slack channel (cost delta can be large).

Kai (SRE): Escalation rules (practical):
- If impacted pods > 10% of production latency-critical pods for > 5m -> page Kai (SRE) + infra lead.
- If autoscaler fails to replenish capacity within 15m -> open incident, include `gcloud/az/aws` region logs and node-group IDs.
- If repeated preemptions > 3x in 1h for same AZ -> consider AZ drain + migration, escalate to cloud infra.

Maya (infra): 6) Post-event actions (do within 24h):
- Run `spot-evac` diagnostic script and attach output to ticket.
- Add preemption sample to the eval set to detect regressions.
- Review pool sizing and cushion; set `min_nodes` to cover the critical reserved capacity.

Sam (oncall): Where is the script?

Jordan (eng-infra): `/opt/runbooks/spot-evac.sh` on jumpbox and `/playbooks/spot-recovery.md` in the repo. Use `./spot-evac.sh --summary` and paste output.

Maya (infra): Handy commands (copyable):
```
# list spot nodes
kubectl get nodes -l pool=spot -o wide
# drain single node safely
kubectl cordon node-123 && kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# show pods evicted
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.reason=="Evicted") | {name:.metadata.name, ns:.metadata.namespace}'
```

Kai (SRE): Add: if you see repeated OOMKilled on model containers after reschedule, bump ephemeral storage or pin to larger instance type; tagging helps finance attribution.

Maya (infra): Communication blurbs:
- Short Slack update: "inc: spot churn eu-west-1 impacting prod-models; shifted critical traffic to dedicated-fallback; autoscaler rehiring nodes; monitoring. Paging Kai if degradation continues."
- Postmortem title: "spot preemption surge — <region/date>" include node-group id, preemption timestamps, and mitigation timeline.

Sam (oncall): Thanks — saving this to runbook bookmarks.

Jordan (eng-infra): One more operational best-practice: label jobs with `spot-tolerant=true` or `latency-critical=true` so autoscaler and admission can make smarter placement decisions.

Maya (infra): Final: quick checklist at glance:
- [ ] confirm scope (ops-bot)
- [ ] check pods/nodes and autoscaler status
- [ ] allow autoscaler 3–7m unless >5% impact
- [ ] drain in small batches if manual rescue needed
- [ ] flip routes to dedicated-fallback for latency-critical services
- [ ] escalate per rules above

ops-bot: note: auto-archive thread in 7d unless pinned.

Kai (SRE): pinned.

Sam (oncall): on it, will run `spot-evac.sh --summary` now and paste results if anything weird.
